Functional Requirements Summary: FR-1: One Follow300 policy lives in src/strategy/ with no Nautilus, polymaker, pandas, filesystem, network, or system-clock dependencies
FR-2: Backtest and live/paper adapters call that core; a strategy change in this branch reaches both consumers in one code update

FR-3: Same initial state, settings, and inbound event order produce the same core decisions, orders, and reject reasons; fill/PnL may still differ because queue, data source, latency, trade confirms, and wallet come from outside

FR-4: level_usdc is a required session input. Four independent adapter-config values: backtest Dota $100, backtest LoL $100, live/paper Dota $65, live/paper LoL $20. Core has no game or mode constants
FR-5: One latched token per episode; up to three open BUY rungs at $0.01; BUY and one SELL may rest together; an open position does not block BUY
FR-6: Mid-episode restart is exit-only: cancel restored BUY, wait for cancel/settle outcomes, sell the verified position, no new BUY for that restored map session

FR-7: A new BUY is admitted against a budget snapshot that includes resting, in-flight, and to-be-cancelled BUY across Dota and LoL. Shortfall skips the whole rung; it does not shrink level_usdc. Live/paper dollar caps stay multiples of the two clips so they move when those sizes move
FR-8: Live executes the core plan (keep/cancel/place) through existing Engine seams. The esports path does not run a second generic quote-diff or resize_frac reconcile
FR-9: poly-maker stays frozen. Engine classes and methods are patched from esports-trader only
FR-10: Extraction identity is proven on four seed-0 postcleanup replays before any labeled behavior change. After those changes, a new 12-seed baseline per game is the accepted Follow300 result
Resolved Questions: V1 boundary: stop after both adapters, labeled behavior changes, paper decision traces, and a 12-seed new baseline. VPS drain, deploy, rollback, and merge to main are a later feature. All steps land on ladder-experiment.

Extraction pass bar: fills, place/cancel, episode/level links, reserve size and timestamps on Dota 8837869969, 8911784562, 8933879286 and LoL 115564793879469302, seed 0. Known Nautilus zero-fill faults stay labeled engine faults. PnL is a check, not the only check. Quote-event logs may gain extra core-trace fields; comparison uses the identity fields above, not bit-identical files.

Recalc cadence: the accepted end state is live's clocks in both adapters — debounce_ms=100 on book/signal plus quoter_tick_s=2.0 fallback. Extraction identity still uses today's backtest 1s timer. Switching clocks is a later labeled policy bump with a new 12-seed baseline, because doing it in the first engine commit would break the identity bar.

Live/paper capital: user wallet is ~$1000; both games run at once; user watches HALT by hand and does not want a map-count cap. Keep session_config.py DOLLAR_MULTIPLES (daily_loss_kill 4x, max_total_exposure 8x, max_event_group_loss 4x, max_market_notional 4x, q_max 4x) derived from the two live clips. After clips become level_usdc $65 / $20, that is kill $340, exposure $680, market $340, q_max $260 / $80. Changing the two sizes auto-raises the caps. No extra concurrent-map counter: skip-whole-level on the budget snapshot is the limiter. Resting BUY must count in the snapshot (today they do not in fork exposure).

Restart: already chosen in the spec — exit-only, no new BUY for a restored map session. New maps in the same process still get the full ladder. Old journals that lack rung/order links use the same drain path. Resume-ladder-from-snapshot is out of scope.

SELL table: extract current backtest semantics first (a new BUY fill restarts the 10s settle and the working SELL is cancelled on the next requote). Then a labeled change adopts live MATCHED-unconfirmed hold plus 1s SELL min-life in both adapters, including backtest. That change needs a new baseline; old Follow300 numbers are not a check of the new table.

Late fill of an old episode: current backtest _credit_detached_level_fill matches a rung by index without episode_id. Core implements ownership by episode_id from the start. The 4 identity replays are not this scenario. A labeled step adds the regression (including a different token) and blocks new BUY until unresolved ownership is reconciled.
EVENT cooloff: remove from the esports strategy path. Real HALT, wallet limits, and reduce-only stay as adapter-supplied permissions into the core.
Signal contract: inbound delta is the raw model delta. Live must stop reconstructing clipped_fair - market_p. Anchor gate in live uses the book the signal was computed on, not a dataset price.
Cutoff: adapters pass game-second 540. They do not convert cutoff into data-delay or network-latency time.
min_order_size: same market-limits struct in both adapters. Live uses market metadata. Backtest 5 shares when history has no metadata, flagged on the manifest.

PaperGateway PnL is not a queue/partial-fill equivalence check against the historical simulator. Equivalence is same synthetic tape → same core state and commands, plus the paper decision-trace replay.
Full historical shared-wallet fill-path rerun under a tight $1000 budget is out of scope. This feature adds contract scenarios with a fake tight budget and replays decisions under identical limits.
poly-maker: frozen. No strategy-driver PR to the fork. No edits under ../poly-maker.
Non-Goals (Out of Scope for V1): VPS inspect, drain, enable, rollback, or version-pin deploy
Any file change in ../poly-maker or a strategy-driver API inside the fork
Full historical portfolio simulator that reruns the fill path when shared capital is short
Resume the BUY ladder from a saved snapshot after crash (exit-only only)
Registry of experimental strategies or re-running the discarded strategy grid
Using PaperGateway PnL as proof that live and backtest queues match
